T-001.threat: Process input tampering — attacker modifies input data to alter process behavior
T-001.cause: Insufficient input validation — the process accepts data without verifying its integrity
T-001.attack: Attacker injects malformed or malicious input data that causes the process to behave incorrectly

T-002.threat: Process state tampering — attacker modifies process state to gain unauthorized capabilities
T-002.cause: Process state is stored without integrity protection
T-002.attack: Attacker modifies process state variables to bypass security checks

T-003.threat: Data flow tampering — attacker modifies data in transit between components
T-003.cause: Data flow is unprotected — no integrity check or encryption prevents modification
T-003.attack: Attacker intercepts and modifies values before they reach the destination

T-004.threat: Data flow replay attack — attacker replays captured legitimate messages
T-004.cause: No replay protection on data flow — messages lack sequence numbers or nonces
T-004.attack: Attacker captures a legitimate message and replays it to trigger the same action without authorization

T-005.threat: Data store tampering — attacker modifies stored data to alter system behavior
T-005.cause: Data store lacks access controls or integrity protection
T-005.attack: Attacker modifies configuration, state, or security parameters in the data store

T-006.threat: Data store injection — attacker injects malicious data into the data store
T-006.cause: No input sanitization before writing to the data store
T-006.attack: Attacker writes malicious payloads that are later executed by other system components

T-007.threat: System configuration tampering — attacker modifies system configuration
T-007.cause: System configuration is stored without integrity protection or access control
T-007.attack: Attacker modifies configuration parameters to disable security controls or create backdoors
